full_judgment:
2. The appellant as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 61 of 1964 in the Court of Munsif, Fatickchari claiming title to the suit land on the basis of pattan from the landlords. R.S. Plot No.3226 appertaining to R.S. Khatian No. 1234 of mouza Uttar Rangamatia, P.S. Fatickchari is the subject matter of the suit. Ram Kamal Saha and others admittedly were the landlords. Plaintiff alleged that he was in possession and that defendants had been threatening to dispossess him. The defendants (the respondents here) contested the suit alleging inter alia that the disputed land was taken settlement of by their predecessor Abdul Ali by a patta dated 5th Jaistha, 1207 M.E. They claimed to be in possession since the time of their predecessor. The learned Munsif decreed the suit. On appeal the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong, who heard the appeal, reversed the decision of the learned Munsif and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff has moved this Court and obtained the present rule. 

 3. Mr. Shahadat Hossain learned advocate for the appellant has taken me through the judgments of Courts below and other materials on record. The learned advocate submits that the judgment of the lower appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal. According to the learned advocate, the defendants had failed to prove that the suit land was identical with the land they claimed on the strength of patta and on the evidence adduced by the plaintiff, the plaintiff was entitled to a decree. The learned advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has erred in law in taking the view that the recent record of right the P.S. Khatian which stands in the name of the plaintiff is incorrect. He also submits that the presumptive value of the khatian has not been rebutted. 

 5. It appears from the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge that he has come to a conclusion on a careful consideration of the evidence on record that the plaintiff has failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit relying on the principle that the plaintiff must succeed on his own case and cannot be allowed to succeed by taking advantage of any defects in the defence. In the instant case the trial cowl found fault with the defendants in as much as they had failed to get the patta Ext. B relayed through a local investigation, but it is evident that the failure of the defendants could not negatively prove plaintiffs' title and posse lion in the suit-land and crown him with a decree. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge has, on a proper appreciation of the evidence, oral and documentary, came to the conclusion that the plaintiff had failed to prove his title and possession, and, for the matter of that, plaintiff had no title and possession and no error of law could be pointed out in the learned Subordinate Judge's arrival at this finding and decision. His judgment can by no means be assailed as not being a proper judgment of reversal. The only point that requires examination is whether the learned Subordinate Judge has erred in law in holding that the P.S. Khatian Ext. 1 standing in the name of the plaintiff is incorrect. It appears that in corning to this conclusion the learned Subordinate Judge has relied on Exts. B, B(l) and B(2), three previous judgment as well as the oral evidence adduced by the parties. I find it difficult to hold the learned Subordinate Judge responsible for committing an error of law in holding that the P.S. Khatian is incorrect. Mr. Shahadat Hossain learned advocate has submitted that Ext.1, the P.S. Khatian has a presumption in favour of the plaintiff in as much as it records possession of the plaintiff in the suit-land. The P.S. Khatian was prepared under Chapter IV of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and sub-section (3) of section 19 provides that final publication of a record of right under section 19 shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under that Chapter. Sub-section (3) does not provide that record of right prepared under Chapter IV shall have any presumption as to the correctness of the entries made therein in this connection it will be profitable to refer to section 144A of the S.A. & T. Act Section. 144A provides that every entry in a record of right prepared or revised under Section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. The presumption of correctness that has been attached to an entry in a record of right prepared or revised under section 144 has not been attached to an entry in a record of right prepared or revised under Chapter IV. To say that the entry in a record of right prepared under Chapter IV has a presumption of correctness is to read something into the statute which is not there in it and this, the Court cannot do. In the case of Khirod Chandra Das and others V. Bhuti Ram Das and ors. reported in 19 D.L.R.9, the erstwhile Dhaka High Court held that "sub-section (3) of section 19 was conclusive evidence as regards due preparation and revision of the record but it is not certainly conclusive evidence of the state of things appearing in the record or right, or in other words, it is not conclusive evidence of the correctness of the entices in the record of right. It is just a piece of evidence as any other evidence without any presumption of correctness". I am in respectful agreement with the view expressed in the decision. I am therefore unable to find fault with the judgment of the learned lower appellate court if it has after considering the P.S. Khatian Ext.1 in the light of the other evidence on record has come to a conclusion that Ext.1 is incorrect. In doing so, the learned lower appellate court has not committed any illegality. There is no substance in this appeal.
